text:
Sam Cooper: Quick question — for the new token model I'm prototyping: should we bind short-lived tokens to org-level or project-level scopes by default? Thinking about quota attribution + routing fallback. cc @Maria @Aj

Maria Lin: My vote is project-scoped by default. Most customers want per-project billing/quotas. Org-scope for org-admin workflows only.

Aj Patel: Project default makes sense. But we need an easy way to escalate to org scope without creating new token types. Maybe a flag on creation: `scope: project|org` and an audit tag.

Diego Ramos: +1 to project default. Also: telemetry — we must emit both token_id and resolved_scope in traces so console dashboards can roll up correctly.

Neha Singh: Important: routing policies rely on scope for model routing (e.g., dedicated vs hosted). If token is org-scoped and the project pinned a dedicated pool, we need deterministic rules. Proposed: project pin wins, org pin only if project has no override.

Sam Cooper: Good point Neha. So routing precedence: explicit project routing > org routing > global defaults. Add to spec.

Maria Lin: UX question: How do orgs see a project's tokens in Console? We shouldn't expose raw tokens across org viewers. Can show metadata and rotation status, not value.

Aj Patel: Console generation flow sketch: 1) choose service account or user 2) select scope (project/org) 3) choose TTL (15m, 1h, 24h, custom) 4) optionally enable one-click rotate 5) show telemetry onboarding snippet.

Neha Singh: On quotas: should we deduct quota from project bucket when token is org-scoped but used for a project resource? I'd expect yes (attribution to where compute happened). Otherwise customers get surprise bills.

Diego Ramos: Implementation note: we can stamp resolved_project_id on the request at edge after auth. That lets billing/telemetry attribute correctly even for org tokens. Edge does auth -> emit resolved_project_id.

Sam Cooper: Nice. How about service accounts vs user tokens? Service tokens should default to longer TTLs and have rotation hooks; user tokens shorter TTL, interactive UX for rotation.

Maria Lin: Agree. Also add a "least-privilege" checkbox in the Console when creating tokens to default perms to the minimum set.

Aj Patel: API surface: POST /v1/tokens {subject_id, subject_type, scope, ttl_minutes, perms: []}. Response returns token_id, secret (only once). We need strong helper docs about secret storage.

Neha Singh: Must add telemetry event `token.created` with fields: token_id, subject_type, subject_id (hashed), scope, ttl, requested_perms. Also `token.revoked`, `token.rotated`. All PII hashed.

Sam Cooper: Who owns the telemetry dashboard? Product or Platform? We need a dedicated per-org token telemetry view plus cross-org aggregated metrics for SRE.

Maria Lin: Product should own the user-facing dashboards. Platform owns raw telemetry streams and infra-level dashboards (latency, error rates by token resolution path).

Diego Ramos: Rolling this out: feature-flagged canary: `auth.scoped_tokens_v2`. Start with 5% of orgs, opt-in via Console. Provide migration tool that can convert legacy keys into scoped tokens (TTL + resolved scope).

Aj Patel: Migration caveat: legacy keys that are effectively org-admin should be mapped to org-scoped tokens; but we should require an explicit ack in Console before converting to avoid breaking automation.

Neha Singh: From quotas POV: we need a backfill plan for historical usage attribution when converting tokens for billing. Otherwise customers see mismatches for the billing period.

Sam Cooper: Ops question: can we support token pinning to dedicated pools? Means tokens carry `preferred_pool_id` claim. If pool unavailable, fallback to routing precedence.

Diego Ramos: Technically fine. Add `preferred_pool_id` to token metadata and ensure the fallback policy is enforced at the router. Telemetry should record whether preferred pool used or fallback occurred.

Maria Lin: Small UX nit: in Console when a token triggers fallback, show a small banner on the token detail: "Requests were routed to fallback pool X times in the last 24h" with a link to pooled metrics.

audit-bot: audit-bot: New token created (token_id=tok_3a7f, subject=service-account:infra-deploy, scope=project:infra)

Sam Cooper: Good test. For rollout checklist: docs, API, Console changes, router support, billing attribution, telemetry events, migration playbook, canary flag. Who wants to own the playbook?

Aj Patel: I'll own the API + migration playbook. Maria take Console. Diego take router + telemetry. Neha take billing attribution. Sam will coordinate rollout and SLO updates.

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: canary flag `auth.scoped_tokens_v2` enabled for orgs [alpha-org-5] by Aj Patel

Sam Cooper: Thanks team — I'll draft the RFC with the routing precedence, telemetry schema, and migration steps and ping for review tomorrow. :+1:
